title: Inheritance and Letter
premise: Retired detective Ivo Winterbourne finds a stranger dead in their bookshop, dressed in Ivo's own clothes and clutching a letter bearing the seal of the Harrowgate case — the unsolved inheritance murder that ended Ivo's career twenty years ago. The letter, written by the original victim, names a second heir who was never found, and reveals that the man convicted was innocent. As Ivo reopens the case against the wishes of the powerful Winterbourne-adjacent family who buried it, they discover the dead man was the missing heir, killed to keep the fortune — and the old cover-up — intact. In the end, Ivo exposes the surviving conspirator at a public reading of the victim's letter, choosing justice outside the law over arrest, and closes the bookshop to finally leave the past behind.
about_author: Orsen Nystrom is the pen name of a former small-town court clerk who spent a decade transcribing testimony before turning to fiction. They write slow-burn mysteries about ordinary people forced to weigh the law against their consciences.

chapters.title: The Borrowed Coat
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Opening the bookshop on a gray morning, Ivo finds a dead man in the back room wearing Ivo's own tweed coat, holding a sealed letter. The police treat Ivo as a witness, then a suspect. Emotional beat: cold dread as recognition dawns — the coat is the one Ivo wore the night of the Harrowgate murder.

chapters.title: A Case Closed for Good
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, with flashbacks. Ivo resists reopening the past, but the letter's wax seal matches documents from the Harrowgate estate murder that destroyed their career. A young constable, Dana Reyes, quietly shares the autopsy: the victim died days ago, elsewhere. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity curdling into obligation.

chapters.title: The Second Heir
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Digging through old case files in a storage basement, Ivo learns the will named two heirs — one convicted of the murder, one vanished before probate. The dead man's fingerprints match the missing heir, Tomas Ellery. Emotional beat: vertigo, realizing the case everyone swore closed was never solved at all.

chapters.title: What the Widow Remembers
chapters.summary: Ivo interviews elderly Maren Voss, widow of the estate's lawyer, who hints her husband altered the will under pressure from the Aldous family. That night the bookshop window is smashed and the letter nearly stolen. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance; Ivo decides to take the case.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV via recovered letters interleaved with Ivo's present-day search. Tomas spent years hiding, gathering proof of his innocence, and mailed the letter to Ivo deliberately — because Ivo was the detective who doubted the conviction. Emotional beat: grief and tenderness; the dead man becomes a person, not a puzzle.

chapters.title: The Family Name
chapters.summary: Ivo confronts Edmund Aldous, patriarch and Ivo's former mentor, who warns them off with veiled threats and an offer: money, silence, restoration of reputation. Reyes warns Ivo she's being watched too. Emotional beat: temptation and disgust — Ivo sees how power buys memory.

chapters.title: Ash in the Archive
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The county archive burns overnight, destroying the original will and evidence. Reyes is suspended for helping Ivo. Alone, Ivo realizes the only remaining proof is the letter itself — and whoever sent the arsonist knows it. Emotional beat: despair, then resolve; the fire confirms guilt rather than erasing it.

chapters.title: Confession in Miniature
chapters.summary: Ivo traces the arsonist to a frightened former estate groundskeeper who confesses he helped stage the original murder scene as a young man, believing he was protecting the family from a thief. He names the true killer's accomplice: Edmund's late brother. Emotional beat: pity for a broken man; the machinery of the cover-up laid bare.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At a memorial event for the town's founding families, Ivo publicly reads Tomas's letter aloud, laying out the forged will, the false conviction, and the decades of silence while Edmund watches. Edmund breaks, half-confessing on record before his lawyers drag him away. Emotional beat: catharsis and terror intertwined — justice done in daylight, outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: Closing Time
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, weeks later. The conviction is posthumously overturned; Tomas is buried under his own name; Reyes, reinstated, brings the final paperwork. Edmund awaits trial, ruined but alive. Ivo sells the bookshop, keeping only the coat and the letter. Emotional beat: quiet, costly peace — survival's price paid, and worth it.
